questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which of the following statements is true regarding the dose-response curve shown in the image below?
options: C is more potent than A
B is more potent than A
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. B is competitive antagonist

In the above image, drug B is a competitive antagonist.

In competitive antagonism, the DRC is shifted to the right whereas in non-competitive antagonism the DRC is flattened.

Thus in the above image Drug B is the Competitive antagonist while drug C is the non-competitive antagonist.

Potency:

• It is defined as the amount of drug needed to produce a given response.
• A highly potent drug evokes a given response at low concentrations and vice-versa.
• The more the curve is on the left in a dose-response curve (DRC), the greater is its potency.
• Thus, in the above image, the potency is drug A > drug C > drug B.

Efficacy:

• It is defined as the maximum effect produced by the drug.
• It expresses the effect produced by the receptors when bound by a certain drug.
• In the log dose-response curve, the perpendicular height represents the drug efficacy.
• Thus, in the above image, the efficacy is drug A = drug B > drug C.
questions.learning: B is competitive antagonist — In the above image, drug B is a competitive antagonist. In competitive antagonism, the DRC is shifted to the right whereas in non-competitive antagonism the DRC is flattened.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.text: A patient expired as he has accidentally suffered from an unknown gas poisoning. He had cherry red appearance of his blood at the post-mortem finding. Which of the following is the likely cause of his death?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Anemic hypoxia

Cherry red coloration of blood is characteristic of carbon monoxide poisoning, where CO binds hemoglobin with high affinity forming carboxyhemoglobin.

This reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood, despite normal PaO₂, producing anemic hypoxia.

| Option | Type of Hypoxia | Mechanism | When it is Correct | Why NOT Correct Here | Exam Pearl

| ------ | --------------- | --------- | ------------------ | -------------------- | ----------

| A. Hypoxic hypoxia | ↓ PaO₂ | High altitude, lung disease | Low oxygen in blood | ❌ PaO₂ may be normal in CO poisoning | Cyanosis present

| B. Histotoxic hypoxia | Cells can’t use O₂ | Cyanide poisoning | Mitochondrial poisoning | ❌ Blood O₂ normal, no cherry red | Venous O₂ high

| C. Anemic hypoxia ✅ | ↓ O₂-carrying capacity | CO poisoning, anemia | ✔ Hb ineffective | ✔ Correct | Cherry-red hallmark

| D. Ischemic hypoxia | ↓ blood flow | Shock, heart failure | Perfusion problem | ❌ Not Hb issue | Local hypoxia
questions.learning: Anemic hypoxia Cherry red coloration of blood is characteristic of carbon monoxide poisoning, where CO binds hemoglobin with high affinity forming carboxyhemoglobin.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: A 54-year-old comes to the casualty with a history of massive hemoptysis. His routine investigation and chest X-ray were normal. Which of the following you will not do to prevent hemoptysis?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Procoagulant drugs

Procoagulant drugs are not used to prevent hemoptysis. Procoagulant drugs like vasopressin are indicated only if there is an abnormal coagulation profile.

Massive hemoptysis is generally defined as the expectoration of over 600 mL of blood within a 24-h period.

Treatment priorities in the management of massive hemoptysis:

• First priorities are to secure the airway, optimize oxygenation and stabilize the hemodynamic status by administering IV fluids.
• Chest X-ray is the first investigation of choice. CT scan is done only in hemodynamically stable patients.
• If the bleeding site is known, the patient should be placed in a lateral decubitus position with the bleeding side down to prevent aspiration into the unaffected lung. Supplemental oxygen should be given.
• If large-volume bleeding continues or the airway is compromised, the patient should be intubated and undergo an emergency bronchoscopy.
• The bleeding site is localized using flexible/rigid bronchoscopy.
• Control the hemorrhage:

• Endobronchially with Nd: YAG laser or bronchial occlusion
• Endovascularly with bronchial and/or pulmonary artery embolization
• Electrocauterization
• Surgically with resection of the involved lobe

The cause of the hemoptysis must be determined to definitively prevent a recurrence.
questions.learning: Procoagulant drugs Procoagulant drugs are not used to prevent hemoptysis. Procoagulant drugs like vasopressin are indicated only if there is an abnormal coagulation profile.

questions.subject: Dermatology
questions.text: Considering the disease depicted in the given image, which of the following specimens would not be expected to contain filarial worms?
questions.explanation: The image shows elephantiasis, the chronic stage of lymphatic filariasis caused by Wuchereria bancrofti or Brugia malayi. The adult worms live in the lymphatic system, and the female worms release microfilariae into the host's circulation. Microfilariae can be found in the "blood" (Option A), typically showing nocturnal periodicity. They can also be found in "urine" in patients with chyluria (Option C) or in "hydrocele fluid" (Option D), which is a common manifestation in males. Filarial worms are "not found in saliva" (Option B), as there is no anatomical or physiological mechanism for the worms or microfilariae to enter the salivary secretions. Diagnosis is often made by demonstrating microfilariae in a midnight blood smear or by detecting circulating filarial antigens. Elephantiasis results from chronic lymphatic obstruction and secondary fibrosis. Management involves mass drug administration with diethylcarbamazine (DEC) and albendazole, alongside meticulous local skin hygiene to prevent secondary bacterial infections that worsen the limb swelling
questions.learning: The image shows elephantiasis, the chronic stage of lymphatic filariasis caused by Wuchereria bancrofti or Brugia malayi. The adult worms live in the lymphatic system, and the female worms release microfilariae into the host's circulation.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: A patient with a previous history of trauma now presents with diplopia, epistaxis, and restricted ocular movements. Based on these clinical features and the findings shown on the CT scan, what is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The clinical and radiological findings are pathognomonic for an Orbital Blow-out Fracture. This injury occurs when blunt force to the globe increases intraorbital pressure, causing the thin inferior orbital wall to fracture. The provided CT image shows the definitive "teardrop sign"—the herniation of orbital fat and the inferior rectus muscle into the maxillary sinus. This herniation leads to the patient's limited eye movements (specifically upward gaze) and resultant double vision (diplopia). Epistaxis (nosebleeds) occurs due to the associated fracture of the sinus walls. Le Fort fractures (Option A) involve broader facial bones in specific patterns. Isolated maxillary (Option B) or zygomatic (Option C) fractures would present with different patterns of facial instability. Because the pathology is strictly localized to the floor of the orbit with entrapment of contents as shown on CT, blow-out fracture is the definitive diagnosis
questions.learning: The clinical and radiological findings are pathognomonic for an Orbital Blow-out Fracture. This injury occurs when blunt force to the globe increases intraorbital pressure, causing the thin inferior orbital wall to fracture.

questions.subject: ENT
questions.text: A 45-year-old school teacher presents with hoarseness of voice and vocal fatigue. A flexible laryngoscopic examination is performed, and the image is shown below. Based on the laryngoscopic findings, what is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A 45-year-old teacher presenting with progressive hoarseness and voice fatigue suggests a chronic laryngeal condition. The key diagnostic clue comes from the laryngoscopic image, which shows irregular, white, thickened patches on the vocal cords. These findings are characteristic of keratosis of the larynx (laryngeal leukoplakia). Keratosis larynx is a precancerous condition caused by chronic irritation, such as prolonged voice use (common in teachers), smoking, or exposure to irritants. The lesions appear as white, hyperkeratotic plaques, which are typically irregular and patchy, unlike smooth or symmetrical lesions seen in other conditions. Why other options are incorrect: 1. Vocal nodules → Bilateral, symmetrical lesions at specific junctions 2. Reinke’s edema → Diffuse, bilateral swelling, often in smokers 3. Vocal polyp → Usually unilateral, smooth, and vascular
questions.learning: A 45-year-old teacher presenting with progressive hoarseness and voice fatigue suggests a chronic laryngeal condition. The key diagnostic clue comes from the laryngoscopic image, which shows irregular, white, thickened patches on the vocal cords.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following are correct for managing hypertrophic scars? 1. Silicone gel sheeting 2. Intralesional steroid injections 3. Vitamin A gel applications 4. Laser treatment Select the answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 2 and 4

Hypertrophic scars are raised, erythematous scars confined within the boundaries of the original wound. They result from excess collagen deposition during wound healing and may improve spontaneously over time.

• 1. Silicone gel sheeting ✓

• First-line non-invasive treatment for hypertrophic scars. It hydrates the scar, reduces collagen deposition, and improves scar thickness and erythema.

• 2. Intralesional steroid injections ✓

• Triamcinolone acetonide is the treatment of choice for symptomatic hypertrophic scars. It suppresses fibroblast proliferation and collagen synthesis.

• 3. Vitamin A gel applications ✗

• Vitamin A preparations are not standard evidence-based therapy for hypertrophic scars.

• 4. Laser treatment ✓

• Pulsed dye laser (PDL) and fractional CO₂ laser improve scar vascularity, thickness, pigmentation, and pliability.
questions.learning: 1, 2 and 4 Hypertrophic scars are raised, erythematous scars confined within the boundaries of the original wound. They result from excess collagen deposition during wound healing and may improve spontaneously over time. • 1.

questions.subject: Community Medicine
questions.text: Which of the following models of disease causation is depicted in the image below?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Sufficient component cause model

The model of disease causation depicted below is a sufficient component cause model.

It was developed by Rothman based on the idea that an outcome can only happen when a sufficient cause is present. A disease can have multiple sufficient causes. But, each sufficient cause can consist of a pie chart of component causes, a causal pie.  One component cause can be a part of more than one sufficient cause. A component cause can be considered necessary if it is a part of a disease's sufficient causes.

In the given model, each pie chart represents a sufficient cause made of component causes. Since B is present in all the charts, it can be considered a necessary cause. All the others are contributing causes.

Other options:

Option B: An epidemiological triad depicts the interrelationship between the causative agent, the host, and the environment. All of them contribute to disease development. The aim of an epidemiological triad is to identify how to break this relationship and prevent the outbreak of the disease.

Option C: PERT is used for network analysis. It is a type of quantitative management technique that helps in detailed planning and comprehensive supervision.

Option D: The web of causation considers all the predisposing factors and their complex interrelationship with each other. This model is ideally suited to study chronic disease. The web of causation does not imply that the disease is controlled only when all the multiple chains of causation are removed. Sometimes removal of one significant link is sufficient to control the disease.
questions.learning: Sufficient component cause model — The model of disease causation depicted below is a sufficient component cause model. It was developed by Rothman based on the idea that an outcome can only happen when a sufficient cause is present.

questions.subject: Medicine
questions.topic: GI Hepatobiliary System · All Qbank Qs Excluding Pyqs
questions.text: A 54-year-old man with epigastric pain and positive occult blood test undergoes endoscopy, revealing hyperemic nodular mucosa. Biopsy shows submucosal glands producing alkaline mucus. Which part of the GI tract was biopsied?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. First part of the duodenum

Brunner glands are submucosal glands located in the proximal (first part) of the duodenum that secrete alkaline mucus.

The alkaline mucus produced by Brunner glands neutralizes acidic chyme entering the duodenum from the stomach.

This protects the duodenal mucosa and creates an optimal pH for pancreatic enzymes to function.

Key histologic feature: Presence of mucus-secreting submucosal glands is characteristic of the first part of the duodenum and helps distinguish it from other segments of the small intestine.
questions.learning: First part of the duodenum Brunner glands are submucosal glands located in the proximal (first part) of the duodenum that secrete alkaline mucus. The alkaline mucus produced by Brunner glands neutralizes acidic chyme entering the duodenum from the stomach.
